environment.topology: single-host laboratory (docker compose); primary and recovery databases are containers on one machine
environment.disclaimer: Demonstrates the recovery procedure. NOT geographic disaster recovery and NOT evidence of production recovery times.

objectives.note: Planned operation: no data loss is acceptable; the outage is a maintenance window.

summary: Controlled failback completed with a planned outage of 57.6 s and no data loss. Original primary is primary again; the recovery database is a streaming standby.

steps.name: Check preconditions: recovery database is the acting primary
steps.detail: 17 application services are running on the recovery database

steps.name: Record a transaction on the recovery site (must survive the failback)
Record the final write position of the recovery database
Rebuild the original primary as a standby of the recovery database
Wait until the original primary has replayed every change
Promote the original primary and retire the recovery database from the primary role
steps.detail: original primary promoted; recovery database stopped

steps.name: Rebuild the recovery database as a standby of the original primary
steps.detail: recovery database is a streaming standby again

steps.name: Start application services against the original primary
Validate: nothing was lost and the platform works
steps.detail: pre-failback transaction present; new application APP-2026-000036 approved end to end

timing.explanation: Planned outage: from stopping the services to all services ready on the original primary.

limitations: Both nodes were re-cloned with pg_basebackup, which is practical only for small databases; production would use pg_rewind or a planned switchover of a healthy replica.
Single host: no cross-site transfer time is included.
